'''Michal Lipson''' (born 1970) is an American-Israeli-Brazilian physicist known for her work on [[silicon photonics]]. A member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] since 2019 and the [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 2025, Lipson was named a 2010 [[MacArthur Fellow]] for contributions to silicon photonics especially towards enabling GHz silicon active devices.<ref name="Macfound.org">{{cite web |url=http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.6241257/k.9A04/Michal_Lipson.htm |title=Michal Lipson – MacArthur Foundation |publisher=Macfound.org |date= |access-date=2010-09-29 |archive-date=2010-10-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101003030108/http://www.macfound.org/site/c.lkLXJ8MQKrH/b.6241257/k.9A04/Michal_Lipson.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Until 2014, she was the Given Foundation Professor of Engineering at [[Cornell University]] in the school of electrical and computer engineering and a member of the Kavli Institute for Nanoscience at Cornell.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://nanophotonics.ece.cornell.edu/team.html#michal |title=Cornell Nanophotonics Group – Team |publisher=nanophotonics.ece.cornell.edu |date= |access-date=2010-09-29 |archive-date=2010-08-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100810034232/http://nanophotonics.ece.cornell.edu/team.html#michal |url-status=dead }}</ref> She is now the Eugene Higgins Professor of Electrical Engineering at [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ee.columbia.edu/michal-lipson|title=Michal Lipson &#124; Electrical Engineering|website=www.ee.columbia.edu|access-date=2022-12-09|archive-date=2022-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209092635/https://www.ee.columbia.edu/michal-lipson|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2009 she co-founded the company PicoLuz, which develops and commercializes silicon nanophotonics technologies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.picoluz.com/about/|title=About PicoLuz – PicoLuz|website=www.picoluz.com|access-date=2016-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113040033/http://www.picoluz.com/about/|archive-date=2016-11-13}}</ref><ref name="lipson.ee.columbia.edu">{{Cite web|url=http://lipson.ee.columbia.edu/people/people-taxonomy/faculty|title=Faculty {{!}} Lipson Nanophotonics Group|website=lipson.ee.columbia.edu|access-date=2016-11-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161025143430/http://lipson.ee.columbia.edu/people/people-taxonomy/faculty|archive-date=2016-10-25}}</ref> In 2019, she co-founded Voyant Photonics, which develops next generation lidar technology based on silicon photonics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://voyantphotonics.com/|title=Voyant|website=Voyant|access-date=2022-12-09|archive-date=2022-12-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209092635/https://voyantphotonics.com/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2022, Lipson was a co-founder of Xscape photonics to accelerate [[Artificial intelligence|AI]], [[Machine learning|ML]], and simulation hardware. In 2020 Lipson was elected the 2021 vice president of [[Optica (society)|Optica]] (formerly the Optical Society), and she served as the Optica president in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=15 September 2020|title=OSA News Releases|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2020/silicon_photonics_pioneer_michal_lipson_elected_20/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918114547/https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2020/silicon_photonics_pioneer_michal_lipson_elected_20/|archive-date=18 September 2020|website=The Optical Society}}</ref>

==Education==
Lipson was born in [[Haifa]], Israel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-03-21 |title=The Lipsons manage dual careers by 'synchronizing' education and research and refusing to compromise |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2007/03/synchronizing-hod-and-michal-lipson-manage-dual-careers |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=Cornell Chronicle |language=en}}</ref> After spending two years as an undergraduate student at the Instituto de Física at the [[University of São Paulo]], she continued at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]], where she earned a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in physics in 1992, followed by an [[Master of Science|MSc]] in 1994 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1998, both also in physics.<ref>[https://lipson.ee.columbia.edu/sites/lipson.ee.columbia.edu/files/content/michal_cv_bio/CV_LIPSON_2021.pdf CV Lipson] - website of [[Columbia University in the City of New York]]</ref> Her doctoral research focused on "Coupled Exciton-Photon Modes in Semiconductor Optical Microcavities". Lipson then spent 2 years as a postdoctoral associate with [[Lionel Kimerling]] at [[MIT]], and then accepted a position at [[Cornell University]] in 2001.

==Career and research==
Lipson is best known for her work on silicon photonics. She developed (along with other researchers around the world at IBM, Intel, Ghent University) silicon photonic components such as waveguide couplers, ring resonators, modulators, detectors, WDM wavelength sources and sensors on silicon platform. She published the first paper on a class of versatile waveguides known as [[Slot-waveguide]]s in 2004,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nanophotonics.ece.cornell.edu/Publications/voidNanostructure.pdf |title=Guiding and confining light in void nanostructure |access-date=2008-12-04 |archive-date=2007-06-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070629130103/http://nanophotonics.ece.cornell.edu/Publications/voidNanostructure.pdf }}</ref> which has since been cited over one thousand times. In all her work has been cited 32,373 times (as of January 18, 2018).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?start=0&q=Michal+Lipson+&hl=en&as_sdt=0,5|title = Google Scholar}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=April 2023}} She was also the first to demonstrate [[optical parametric gain]] in silicon,<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Nature |title=Access: Broad-band optical parametric gain on a silicon photonic chip |journal=Nature |volume=441 |issue=7096 |pages=960–963 |doi=10.1038/nature04932 |pmid=16791190 |year=2006 |bibcode=2006Natur.441..960F |s2cid=205210957 }}</ref> which was considered an important step towards building optical amplifiers in silicon.

Lipson's McArthur fellowship <ref name="Macfound.org"/> citation mentions her work in ring modulators (circular waveguides) as the key contribution of Lipson via the continued refinement of both opto-electronic and purely optical circuits for smaller size,<ref name="mani_2010">{{cite journal
  |title = Ultra-low voltage, ultra-small mode volume silicon microring modulator
  |journal = [[Opt. Express]]
  |year = 2010
  |volume = 18
  |issue = 17
  |doi = 10.1364/OE.18.018235
  |pmid = 20721214
  |pages = 18235–18242
  |author1=Sasikanth Manipatruni |author2=Kyle Preston |author3=Long Chen |author4=Michal Lipson |bibcode = 2010OExpr..1818235M |doi-access = free
  }}
.</ref> increased efficiency, and accelerated switching speed <ref name="xu_2007">{{Cite book
  |chapter= High Speed Carrier Injection 18&nbsp;Gbit/s Silicon Micro-ring Electro-optic Modulator
  |year = 2007
  |doi = 10.1109/LEOS.2007.4382517
  |volume = 
  |pages=537–538
  |author1=Sasikanth Manipatruni |author2=Qianfan Xu |author3=Brad Schmidt |author4=Jagat Shakya |author5=Michal Lipson |title = LEOS 2007 - IEEE Lasers and Electro-Optics Society Annual Meeting Conference Proceedings
 |isbn = 978-1-4244-0924-2
  |s2cid = 26131159
 }}
.</ref> The resulting silicon-based photonic integrated circuits have the potential to improve signal transmission and processing dramatically.

Lipson has received numerous honors, including being the recipient of a [[Fulbright Fellowship]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cies.org/schlr_directories/usdir07/Engi19.htm |title=2007 – 2008 U.S. Scholar Directory: Engineering |access-date=2008-12-05 |website=[[Fulbright Scholar Program]] web site |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081009231151/http://www.cies.org/schlr_directories/usdir07/Engi19.htm |archive-date=2008-10-09 }}</ref> and an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Award]]. She is also an elected fellow of Optica. Her current research interests include optical metamaterials, low-power and compact [[optical modulators]], and [[slot waveguide]]s. Her work has appeared in ''Nature'', ''Nature Photonics'', and other journals.
